message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole (AITA) for wanting to back out of the promise I made to my wife after our affair. Let me start by understanding the situation. First, I cheated on my wife, which is a big deal. I took responsibility for that, which is good. When I came clean, she said she'd stay with me if I agreed to make the next year all about her. I agreed because I thought it meant doing things like massages, shopping, and her favorite activities. But instead, she decided the year should be all about Disney. Now, I didn't realize she was that into Disney. I thought she was just into it because our daughters loved it when they were little, but they're grown up now. So, she's made me go to Disneyland seven times this year and Harry Potter World once. I guess Harry Potter is related to Disney now, so that makes sense. She also made me cosplay as Disney characters, including a Beauty and the Beast costume that cost $800. Plus, she makes me watch Frozen every day, and when I asked to change it, she put on Pocahontas 2. I know this isn't as bad as the pain of being cheated on, but I'm really miserable. I can't keep doing this. I want to have an intervention where we stop all the Disney stuff and just go to counseling, which we should have done a while ago. Am I being an asshole for wanting to back out? Hmm, so I need to figure out if my desire to stop the Disney stuff and focus on counseling is justified or if I'm being unreasonable. Let's break it down. First, I made a promise to make the year about her. She chose Disney, which I didn't expect. I went along with it, but it's causing me a lot of stress and unhappiness. I'm spending a lot of money on Disney trips and costumes, and I'm forced to watch the same movies repeatedly. This is affecting my mental health, and I feel like we're not addressing the real issues from the affair. On the other hand, she's trying to heal by focusing on something she enjoys. Maybe she feels that by making me participate, she's ensuring I'm paying attention to her and our relationship. But it's not working for me, and I feel like we're stuck in a cycle that's not helping us move forward. I also feel like we're avoiding the necessary counseling, which is crucial for rebuilding trust and working through the pain of the affair. Without counseling, I'm worried we won't be able to resolve our issues effectively. So, is it wrong to want to stop the Disney stuff and focus on counseling? I think it's more about whether my needs and the health of our relationship are being addressed. I'm not happy, and I'm not sure she is either, despite her focus on Disney. I also need to consider whether I'm being selfish. I made a promise, but it's not sustainable for me. Maybe I should communicate my feelings instead of just wanting to back out. But I'm at the point where I can't continue, so I need to find a way to address this without feeling like I'm being an asshole. In the end, I think it's important to prioritize our relationship's health, which means addressing the underlying issues through counseling. I might not be wrong to want to stop the Disney stuff if it's causing more harm than good. But I should approach this conversation with empathy and understanding, acknowledging her needs while expressing mine.
